key_insight: Urban carbon intensity from PV-dominated grids varies sharply in space and time, so local resolution is essential for accurate emissions-aware control.
engineering_relevance: This enables smarter optimization of building control, EV charging, and district heating by using district-level carbon intensity estimates instead of coarse city averages.
method: Compute spatially and temporally resolved carbon intensity factors at urban district scale.
Train transferable surrogate models using limited census/grid-cell inputs.
Compare decision-tree methods with a neural-network architecture for estimation accuracy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports carbon intensity values ranging from 0 to 316 g/kWh within one city at summer noon, and a case study shows up to 9% emission-estimation error when local variation is ignored.
watch_item: Performance may drop in regions with sparse or incomplete input data, so transferability should be validated before deployment.
paper_title: Quantification and Surrogate Model Estimation of Spatial-Temporal Carbon Intensity Factors
